# Exercises

**Goal:** Use the [Census API user guide](https://www.census.gov/data/developers/guidance/api-user-guide.html) to obtain data from the American Community Survey (ACS) and practice writing functions that interact with APIs.

1. Write a function called `get_acs1()` that gets 1-year ACS data for a given year for a set of user specified variables for all states. Function arguments should include:
    - `year`: Within your function check that this is between 2005 and 2022 and not 2020 (data only available from 2005-2022 except for 2020). If the year is outside this range, include `stop("Helpful error message here")` to display a helpful error message to the user.
    - `variables`: A character vector of variable names to obtain. e.g., `c("B02015_009", "B01003_001")`. Note that these don't have "E" or "M" at the end. You'll always return the "E" version (for the estimate). See next argument for the "M" version. Make sure your function can also handle variables like `NAME`.
    - `include_moe`: TRUE/FALSE indicator of whether to additionally include the "M" version (for the margin of error on the estimate). Set the default to TRUE.
    - `key`: Census API key (if you have trouble getting a key, email the instructor as soon as possible)
    Your function should include a `Sys.sleep(0.5)` at the beginning to pause code execution for 0.5 seconds. While the Census API does not seem to have a [rate limit](https://www.census.gov/data/developers/guidance/api-user-guide.Help_&_Contact_Us.html) when you provide an API key, include this pause just to be safe.
    
```{r}
library(httr2)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
census_api_key <- "3f5a1a31268c926966a79501a486ac42455dd480"
get_acs1 <- function(year, variables, include_moe = TRUE, key) {
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  if (year==2020 || year > 2022 || year < 2005) {
    stop("Input 'year' must be a single numeric value between 2005 and 2022 (excluding 2020)")
  }
  if (length(variables) == 0) {
    stop("Input 'variables' is empty")
  }
  vars <- character(0)
  for (var in variables) {
    if (startsWith(var, "Estimate!!") || startsWith(var, "Margin of Error!!")){
      temp_url <- paste0("https://api.census.gov/data/", year, "/acs/acs1/variables.json")
      tryCatch({
      temp_req <- request(temp_url)
      temp_resp <- req_perform(temp_req)
      temp_data <- resp_body_json(temp_resp, simplifyVector = TRUE)$variables
      lookup <- setNames(names(temp_data), sapply(temp_data, `[[`, "label"))
      })
      var <- lookup[var]
      var <- str_sub(var, end = -2)
    } else if (endsWith(var,"E") || endsWith(var, "M")){
      var <- str_sub(var, end = -2)
    }
    vars <- append(vars, as.character(paste0(var, "E")))
    if (include_moe == TRUE) {
      vars <- append(vars, as.character(paste0(var, "M")))
    }    
  }
  processed_vars <- paste(unlist(vars), collapse = ",")
  base_url <- "https://api.census.gov"
  req <- request(base_url) %>%
        req_url_path_append("data") %>%
        req_url_path_append(year) %>%
        req_url_path_append("acs") %>% 
        req_url_path_append("acs1") %>% 
        req_url_query(
            get = processed_vars,
            `for` = I("state:*"), 
            key = key
        )
  resp <- try(req_perform(req), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(resp, "try-error")) {
        stop("Failed to perform HTTP request")
  }
  response_data <- try(
        resp_body_json(resp, simplifyVector = TRUE, check_type = FALSE),
        silent = TRUE
    )
  header <- response_data[1, ]
  
  acs_data <- as_tibble(response_data[-1, , drop = FALSE], .name_repair = "minimal")
  names(acs_data) <- header
  acs_data <- acs_data %>%mutate(year = year, .before = 1)
  return(acs_data)
}

```
    


2. Come up with a set of test cases that will **fully** test your function. Update your function as needed as you run your tests. Show output from successful tests on all test cases- make sure they are printed and visible in the HTML.

```{r}
get_acs1(2022,c("B02015_009", "B01003_001"), key = census_api_key)
get_acs1(2022,c("B02015_009", "B01003_001", "Estimate!!Median age --!!Female"), key = census_api_key)
get_acs1(2022, c("B02015_009M", "B01003_001E", "Estimate!!Median age --!!Female"), include_moe = FALSE, key = census_api_key)
get_acs1(2022, c("B02015_009M", "B01003_001E", "Estimate!!Median age --!!Female"), key = census_api_key)
```
```{r deliberate-error, error=TRUE}
get_acs1(2020, c("B02015_009M", "B01003_001E", "Estimate!!Median age --!!Female"), include_moe = FALSE, key = census_api_key)
get_acs1(2025, c("B02015_009M", "B01003_001E", "Estimate!!Median age --!!Female"), include_moe = FALSE, key = census_api_key)
get_acs1(2004, c("B02015_009M", "B01003_001E", "Estimate!!Median age --!!Female"), include_moe = FALSE, key = census_api_key)
```


3. Obtain 1-year ACS data for all states from 2005-2022 (except 2020) for the following two variables: `B01003_001` (total population) and `B06011_001` (Median Income in the Past 12 Months in 2022 Inflation-Adjusted Dollars).
    - Get both the estimate and the margin of error for these two variables.
    - Put all of this information into a single data frame.
    - Do this with both a `for` loop and with an appropriate `purrr` function. (See our iteration day 2 activity for reference.)
    - Verify using the `identical()` function that you get identical data frames from both approaches.

For loop:
```{r}
library(purrr)
years <- setdiff(c(2005:2022), 2020)
all_data_list <- list()
for (yr in years) {
  data_of_year <- get_acs1(
      year = yr,
      variables = c("B01003_001", "B06011_001"),
      key = census_api_key
    )
    all_data_list[[as.character(yr)]] <- data_of_year
}
acs_data_loop <- bind_rows(all_data_list, .id = "year") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))%>% 
  arrange(year, state)
acs_data_loop
```

purrr:
```{r}
all_data_list_purrr <- map(years, function(yr) {
    data_of_year <- get_acs1(
      year = yr,
      variables = c("B01003_001", "B06011_001"),
      key = census_api_key)
    return(data_of_year)})
acs_data_purrr <- bind_rows(all_data_list_purrr, .id = "year_index")%>%
mutate(
    year = years[as.integer(year_index)], 
    year = as.integer(year) 
  ) %>%
  select(-year_index)%>% 
  arrange(year, state)
acs_data_purrr
```

check:
```{r}
identical(acs_data_loop,acs_data_purrr)
```


4. Create two separate visualizations that show how the two variables have changed over 2005-2022 (except 2020).
    - Show both the estimate and margin of error (if relevant) in an effective way.
    - Make sure that your plots have clean labels and a title.
    
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
population_data <- acs_data_loop %>%
  select(-"B06011_001E",-"B06011_001M")%>%
  rename("estimate_population" = "B01003_001E")%>%
  rename("moe_population" = "B01003_001M")%>%
  mutate(year=as.character(year),
         estimate_population=as.numeric(estimate_population),
         moe_population=as.numeric(moe_population))
population_data

income_data <- acs_data_loop %>%
  select(-"B01003_001E",-"B01003_001M")%>%
  rename("estimate_income" = "B06011_001E")%>%
  rename("moe_income" = "B06011_001M")%>%
  mutate(year=as.character(year),
         estimate_income=as.numeric(estimate_income),
         moe_income=as.numeric(moe_income))
income_data
```
    
```{r}
library(scales)
ggplot(population_data, aes(x = year, y = estimate_population)) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue", color = "darkblue") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = estimate_population - moe_population, ymax = estimate_population + moe_population),
    width = 0.3,
    color = "darkred",
    linewidth = 0.8
   ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::comma,
      limits = c(0, NA) 
      ) +
  labs(
    title = "Population Trend with Margin of Error", 
    subtitle = "Years 2005-2022 (excluding 2020)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Estimated Population",
    caption = "Data source: US Census Bureau ACS 1-Year Estimates\nError bars represent the Margin of Error (MOE)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))
```
    
```{r}
library(scales)
ggplot(income_data, aes(x = year, y = estimate_income)) +
  geom_col(fill = "skyblue", color = "darkblue") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = estimate_income - moe_income, ymax = estimate_income + moe_income),
    width = 0.3,
    color = "darkred",
    linewidth = 0.8
   ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::comma,
      limits = c(0, NA) 
      ) +
  labs(
    title = "Income Trend with Margin of Error", 
    subtitle = "Years 2005-2022 (excluding 2020)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Estimated Income",
    caption = "Data source: US Census Bureau ACS 1-Year Estimates\nError bars represent the Margin of Error (MOE)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))
```
